newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says U.S. rate hike won't stop bond float.
newsitem.headline: Manila says U.S. rate hike won't stop bond float.

text.p: The Philippines will go ahead with its planned Yankee bond issue this April despite the move by the U.S. Federal Reserve to raise interest rates, the Central Bank said.

Bank Governor Gabriel Singson told reporters at the weekend that April was still "relatively a good time" to proceed with the offering. The issue will be between $750 million and $1.0 billion and have a maturity of at least 30 years.

Singson was reacting to suggestions by some economists to delay the offering because they said the increase in U.S. interest rates would mean higher borrowing costs for Philippine monetary authorities.
The planned float is "like going to the stock market. You don't always get it at the lowest rate," Singson said.

Even if U.S. interest rates are slightly higher now, he said, monetary officials could always offest this by investing the bond proceeds in higher yielding financial instruments in the domestic market.
